extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communicators, and marketers writing press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and distributing press releases that are optimized for search engines and readable for journalists and the public to increase visibility, traffic, and backlinks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pick Your Keywords Wisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about what people would type into Google to find your news; choose keywords with good search volume using tools like Google's Keyword Planner, Ahrefs, or Semrush.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use keyword research tools to find terms with reasonable search volume. Prioritize relevance to the news and to potential readers over chasing high-volume but irrelevant terms. The ultimate goal is to be both search-friendly and reader-friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place main keyword in headline, subheadings, and body
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your main keyword in the headline, in subheadings, and a few times in the text to signal relevance to search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the main keyword thoughtfully (headline + subheads + body) but avoid forcing it. Mix in synonyms and related terms to show topic breadth. Do not obsess over keyword density metrics; natural use is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write Naturally / Avoid Keyword Stuffing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use keywords naturally, don't force them into every sentence; write for readers so the content flows well while still signaling relevance to search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mix in synonyms and related phrases. Watch for awkward or repetitive phrasing caused by keyword insertion. An anti-pattern is cramming the keyword into every sentence; Google can detect unnatural usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: Make Headlines That Pop
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a catchy, clear headline that includes your main keyword and entices clicks; keep it short so it displays well in search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the main keyword and keep the headline under ~70 characters so it looks good in search results. Aim for clarity + interest (not clickbait). The headline should serve both journalists and search users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Subheadings for Skimmability (with keywords)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use subheadings to break up content and include keywords in subheadings to help readability and SEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subheadings make press releases easier to read and help SEO when they include relevant keywords. They also help searchers and journalists scan the story quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link Smartly (limit links)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include 1–2 links to important pages on your site (e.g., homepage or product page) rather than many links which can hurt SEO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't go link-crazy; limit outbound links to the most relevant pages. Ensure links point to useful landing pages and are natural in context. Test links before publishing to avoid broken links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add Visuals with Proper File Names and Alt Text
rubrics_metrics.description: Include images or videos to make the release stand out; use descriptive file names and alt text so search engines understand them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach images/videos to increase engagement. Use descriptive filenames (e.g., keyword-rich but accurate) and fill alt text to improve accessibility and SEO. Avoid decorative images without descriptive metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep It Short and Focused (quality over quantity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer concise, clear writing over long copy; focus on quality rather than maximizing word count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid writing a 'novel' — be straightforward and direct. Use short paragraphs and bullet points to convey key facts quickly. The page explicitly advises against maximizing word-count as an SEO tactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share and Distribute Widely
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a distribution strategy (newswires, social media, direct journalist outreach) so the press release reaches the right people and gains visibility and backlinks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute via reputable channels and post on social media or send directly to journalists. Wider distribution increases chances of pickups and backlinks which help visibility even if press-release links have limited SEO weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for Humans, Not Just Google
rubrics_metrics.description: Prioritize readable, engaging content that serves journalists and stakeholders rather than trying to 'game' search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep tone natural, avoid stuffing keywords, and tell a clear story. The release should be valuable to real readers and to journalists who might republish or write follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a Clear Call-to-Action (CTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell readers what to do next—visit your site, sign up, register, or download—so the release converts attention into action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make CTAs clear, easy to follow, and placed logically in the release. When building relationships with journalists, provide easy-to-share newsroom content to facilitate coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep It Newsworthy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure the press release is timely, relevant, and interesting: press releases are for sharing news, not filler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the story isn't newsworthy it won't grab attention or links. Prioritize genuine news value to attract journalists, bloggers, and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for Easy Reading
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the release skimmable with short paragraphs, bullet points, and plenty of white space so both readers and search engines favor it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use headings, bullets, and clear structure. Skimmable content increases engagement and reduces bounce rate—both positive for visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-Check Everything (proofread and test links)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofread for typos and test every link before publishing because errors and broken links damage credibility and media relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typos and broken links can kill credibility and reduce the chance of coverage. Carefully proofread, validate links, and ensure all contact information is correct.
